intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through pristine alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail passes glacial lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes. Book DOC huts in advance for an overnight experience or tackle a day section from the Routeburn Shelter.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the cruise ships arrive, then hike the Milford Track section through ancient rainforest. Witness towering waterfalls like Stirling Falls up close from your kayak, spot dolphins and seals, and experience the raw wilderness of Fiordland National Park.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike and Beach
experiences.description: Hike the golden coastal trail of Abel Tasman National Park, stopping at pristine turquoise beaches like Anchorage and Bark Bay. The track winds through native bush with stunning sea views, and you can take a water taxi back to Marahau. Swim in crystal-clear waters and spot fur seals along the way.

experiences.name: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Experience a traditional Maori hangi dinner where food is slow-cooked underground using heated rocks, paired with a powerful cultural performance including haka, poi, and waiata (song). Learn about the rich Ngai Tahu heritage of the South Island, hear legends of the land, and enjoy a feast of lamb, chicken, kumara, and vegetables.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Nelson Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect baggage, arrange transfer or budget shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into beachfront accommodation, and rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a late-night convenience store near the resort. Budget option: supermarket snacks or airport food court (~NZD $10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at 22:30 so no activities are planned. Confirm resort has late check-in arrangements. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for affordable data. Exchange some currency or use ATM for NZD cash.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Explore the immediate coastal surroundings and enjoy the fresh sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town centre to stock up on groceries, snacks, and supplies for the trip from a local supermarket (Countdown or Pak'nSave for budget shopping). Pick up a New Zealand hiking map or trail brochure from a local i-SITE visitor information centre.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual sunset walk along the beach. Cook a simple meal at the resort if self-catering facilities are available, or head to a local fish and chips shop for a classic New Zealand budget meal.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket cereal, fruit, and milk purchased locally (~NZD $8-10)
meals.lunch: Supermarket sandwich or bakery pie from a local bakery (~NZD $6-8)
meals.dinner: Local fish and chips shop near the resort (~NZD $10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle orientation day. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline) for South Island navigation. Check weather forecasts for upcoming hiking days. Confirm Abel Tasman hike logistics and any bookings needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning coastal hike along a local beachfront trail near the resort. Explore rock pools, headlands, and scenic lookout points. Bring packed snacks and water. Aim for a 2-3 hour moderate hike to warm up legs for bigger hikes ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for lunch and a rest. Research and book the Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike experience online. Spend the afternoon exploring local beaches and swimming in the sea if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local pub or casual restaurant for dinner. Many New Zealand pubs offer affordable evening meals. Alternatively, cook at the resort using supermarket ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort: toast, eggs, and fruit (~NZD $5-7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch: supermarket bread, cheese, and deli items (~NZD $6-8)
meals.dinner: Local pub meal or casual eatery (~NZD $15-20)

day_by_day.notes: November is late spring in New Zealand so expect warm days and longer daylight hours. Sunscreen and a hat are essential. Check if the resort has a kitchen or communal cooking area to save on meal costs.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by bus or shuttle toward Nelson (if not already based there). Visit the geographic Centre of New Zealand marker and enjoy the short walk up to the hilltop viewpoint overlooking Nelson city and the surrounding bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nelson's vibrant arts and crafts quarter. Browse free galleries and the Nelson Market area. Visit the Nelson i-SITE to gather more hiking information. Walk along the Nelson waterfront and Tasman Bay foreshore.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at one of Nelson's affordable eateries. Nelson has a great food scene with budget-friendly options including Thai, Indian, and local cafes.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort before departure (~NZD $5-7)
meals.lunch: Nelson market food stall or local bakery (~NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Budget ethnic restaurant in Nelson city centre (~NZD $14-18)

day_by_day.notes: Nelson is approximately 1-2 hours from many South Island starting points. Check Intercity or Naked Bus for affordable coach options. Nelson is the gateway to Abel Tasman National Park and is worth at least half a day of exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike and Beach Experience. Depart Nelson early by shuttle or water taxi to the Abel Tasman National Park trailhead at Marahau. Begin hiking the iconic golden coastal trail through native bush, spotting fur seals and seabirds along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Abel Tasman Coast Track, stopping at pristine turquoise beaches including Anchorage or Torrent Bay. Swim in crystal-clear waters, enjoy a packed lunch on the beach, and soak in the stunning coastal scenery. Return via water taxi or continue hiking back to Marahau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nelson or the resort area by late afternoon shuttle. Rest tired legs and enjoy a relaxed dinner. Reflect on the day's incredible coastal hiking experience.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast before departure (~NZD $5-7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from supermarket: sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, and plenty of water (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Casual cafe or self-cooked meal at resort (~NZD $12-16)

day_by_day.notes: The Abel Tasman Coast Track is one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Book the water taxi in advance as it can fill up quickly in summer. Wear sturdy hiking shoes, bring sunscreen, insect repellent, and a rain jacket. Tides affect some sections of the track so check tide tables before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Abel Tasman hike. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Do some gentle stretching or a short beach walk. Plan the next leg of the journey south toward Queenstown, the adventure capital of New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin travel south by InterCity bus or budget rental car toward Westport or Greymouth on the West Coast. The West Coast drive is spectacular with views of the Tasman Sea, rugged cliffs, and native rainforest. Stop at any scenic lookouts along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Greymouth or a West Coast town for the night. Check into a budget hostel or backpacker accommodation. Explore the local area and grab dinner at a local pub.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort (~NZD $5-7)
meals.lunch: Roadside cafe or packed lunch during travel (~NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Local West Coast pub or takeaway (~NZD $12-16)

day_by_day.notes: The West Coast of the South Island is remote and stunning. Fuel up the car before long stretches as petrol stations can be sparse. If using public transport, book InterCity bus tickets in advance for the best budget fares. Budget hostel accommodation will cost approximately NZD $25-40 per night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Franz Josef Glacier or Fox Glacier area. Take a free self-guided walk to the glacier terminal face viewing platform. The glacier valley walk is free and offers incredible views of the ice and surrounding Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Alex Knob Track or Roberts Point Track near Franz Josef for panoramic views of the glacier and coastline. These are free Department of Conservation (DOC) tracks. Alternatively, explore the rainforest walks around Lake Matheson near Fox Glacier for the famous mirror reflection of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Continue south toward Wanaka or Queenstown if time permits, or overnight in Franz Josef village. Enjoy dinner at a local cafe or self-cater with supermarket supplies.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen self-cook or local bakery (~NZD $6-10)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail (~NZD $7-10)
meals.dinner: Franz Josef village cafe or self-catered hostel meal (~NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter and guided glacier walks are available but expensive. The free walking tracks offer excellent value and are highly recommended for budget travellers. Weather can change rapidly in the glacier region so always carry a rain jacket. Lake Matheson is best visited in early morning for mirror reflections.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from the West Coast through Haast Pass toward Wanaka. The Haast Pass road is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand, passing waterfalls, rainforest, and the stunning Blue Pools. Stop at the Blue Pools Walk (30-45 min return) to see crystal-clear turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Wanaka. Explore the lakefront and the famous Wanaka Tree (a lone willow tree growing in Lake Wanaka). Walk along the lake promenade and enjoy the mountain views. Wanaka is a quieter and more affordable alternative to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a Wanaka budget hostel. Explore the town, grab dinner at a local restaurant or takeaway, and plan the next day's activities.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared or hostel breakfast (~NZD $5-8)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop or packed lunch during Haast Pass drive (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Wanaka casual eatery or pizza restaurant (~NZD $14-18)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive takes approximately 3-4 hours from Franz Josef. The Blue Pools are a must-see stop. Wanaka accommodation is generally cheaper than Queenstown. Book ahead for hostel beds in summer as it fills quickly. Wanaka is also a great base for hiking Mount Iron or Roys Peak.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Roys Peak Track near Wanaka. This is one of the most iconic hikes in New Zealand, offering breathtaking panoramic views of Lake Wanaka, Mount Aspiring, and the surrounding Southern Alps. The hike is 16km return with 1,200m elevation gain - allow 5-6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roys Peak hike and reach the summit for incredible views. Take photos at the famous Roys Peak viewpoint. Descend back to the trailhead in the afternoon. The hike is free via the DOC track.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka exhausted but elated. Treat yourself to a well-earned dinner at a local restaurant. Replenish calories after a big day of hiking.

meals.breakfast: Early high-energy breakfast before the hike: oats, banana, and coffee (~NZD $5-8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Roys Peak summit: sandwiches, energy bars, fruit (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Wanaka restaurant or burger joint as a treat (~NZD $16-22)

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is closed during lambing season (October to mid-November) so confirm it is open before departing. Start early (before 7am) to avoid the midday heat and crowds. Bring at least 2 litres of water per person, sunscreen, and layers as the summit can be windy. This is a challenging but rewarding hike.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Wanaka to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour by bus or car). Check into a Queenstown budget hostel or backpacker lodge. Explore the Queenstown waterfront, Steamer Wharf, and the stunning views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Queenstown i-SITE to research and book the bungee jumping experience. Browse the many adventure activity operators. Take the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3-4 hours return) for panoramic views over the town and lake - a great free activity.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's lively bar and restaurant scene. Look for early bird dinner specials or happy hour deals. The Queenstown Night Market (Thursdays) offers affordable street food if timing aligns.

meals.breakfast: Hostel self-cook or Wanaka bakery before departure (~NZD $6-8)
meals.lunch: Queenstown waterfront takeaway or supermarket lunch (~NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Queenstown budget restaurant or food court (~NZD $14-20)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown is the most expensive town on the South Island so budget carefully. Supermarket meals and hostel cooking will save significant money. Look for combo deals on adventure activities. The AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungee is the world's first commercial bungee site and is a must-do for thrill-seekers.

day_by_day.morning: Bungee Jumping at Kawarau Bridge with AJ Hackett Bungy - the world's first commercial bungee jump site, 43 metres above the stunning Kawarau River. Watch other jumpers from the viewing platform before taking the plunge. This is the iconic South Island bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with lunch in Queenstown. In the afternoon, explore the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entrance area or take a walk along the Lake Wakatipu shoreline. Visit the TSS Earnslaw steamship wharf area for free lakeside views.
day_by_day.evening: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience. Enjoy a traditional Maori hangi dinner where food is slow-cooked underground using heated rocks. Experience cultural performances including haka, poi, and traditional storytelling. A meaningful cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: High-energy hostel breakfast before bungee (~NZD $5-8)
meals.lunch: Queenstown casual cafe or takeaway to celebrate the bungee jump (~NZD $12-16)
meals.dinner: Included in the Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience

day_by_day.notes: Book the bungee jump well in advance as slots fill quickly in summer. AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy costs approximately NZD $175-200. The Hangi Feast evening is a highlight of any New Zealand trip and provides authentic cultural immersion. Wear comfortable clothing for both activities. The bungee experience includes viewing the jump on video which can be purchased as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk if not done earlier, or hike the Ben Lomond Track (full day, 11km return, 1,400m elevation) for spectacular views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the surrounding mountains. This is a challenging but rewarding free DOC hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond hike or, if opting for a shorter activity, explore the Queenstown Gardens for free - a beautiful park on a peninsula jutting into Lake Wakatipu. Try the free frisbee golf course in the gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown. Visit the Thursday Night Market on the waterfront for affordable street food from various vendors. Browse local crafts and soak in the vibrant Queenstown atmosphere for the last time.

meals.breakfast: Hostel self-cook: eggs and toast (~NZD $5-7)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch for Ben Lomond hike (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food stalls (~NZD $12-16)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a serious hike requiring good fitness and preparation. Start early and check weather conditions. The gondola can be taken partway up to save time and energy (costs approximately NZD $36 return). Pack plenty of water, snacks, and warm layers as the summit is exposed and can be cold even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Pack bags and check out of the hostel. Take one last walk along the Lake Wakatipu waterfront to enjoy the stunning mountain scenery. Browse any souvenir shops for budget-friendly New Zealand gifts such as postcards or small greenstone pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back toward the resort area or toward the departure airport depending on onward travel plans. If returning to Aegean Bliss Resort for final nights, enjoy a relaxed afternoon on the beachfront. Reflect on 13 incredible days of adventure on the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at Aegean Bliss Resort or near departure point. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a local restaurant. Pack any remaining items and prepare for departure. Review photos and memories from an incredible New Zealand South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final hostel self-cook breakfast or local Queenstown cafe (~NZD $8-12)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside cafe during travel (~NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local restaurant or resort area eatery (~NZD $16-22)

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time for travel on the final day as South Island distances can be deceiving. If flying out of Queenstown, Christchurch, or Nelson, confirm airport transfer arrangements. Queenstown Airport has regular domestic and international connections. Keep some NZD cash for any last-minute purchases or transport costs. This concludes an incredible 13-day budget adventure covering hiking, bungee jumping, Maori culture, glaciers, and stunning coastal scenery.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange airport transfer, and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront accommodation. Freshen up and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport lounge
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or hotel room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival at 22:30, keep Day 1 entirely free of planned activities. Pre-arrange airport transfer or rental car pickup to minimize stress. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance for a smooth late arrival. Rest well for the adventures ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings and soak in the South Island scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest town center on foot or by rental car. Visit a local visitor information center to confirm bookings and gather maps. Browse local shops and pick up any hiking gear or supplies you may need for upcoming adventures.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the resort. Early night to fully recover from jet lag and prepare for the busy days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant or included buffet (~NZD 20-25 if not included)
meals.lunch: Casual cafe lunch in town — try a classic Kiwi meat pie or fish and chips (~NZD 15-20)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the resort — look for a local bistro offering New Zealand lamb or seafood (~NZD 35-50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Do not overplan — jet lag after a long international flight can be significant. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings including the Nevis Bungy, Routeburn Track, and Milford Sound Kayak. Check weather forecasts for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or transfer to Abel Tasman National Park (if based in the Nelson/Marlborough region) or explore the local coastal area with a gentle morning hike. Start with a 2-hour scenic coastal walk near the resort to ease into hiking mode.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike and Beach experience. Hike the golden coastal trail through Abel Tasman National Park, stopping at pristine turquoise beaches. The afternoon light on the golden sand and clear waters is spectacular in November (early summer).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Shower and relax before heading out for dinner. Share stories of the day over a well-earned meal.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the resort to fuel the hike — eggs, toast, fruit (~NZD 20-25)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — prepare sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and energy bars the night before (self-catered ~NZD 10-15)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant or resort dining — try New Zealand green-lipped mussels or a lamb rack (~NZD 40-55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and a hat — November is early summer in New Zealand and UV levels are very high. Bring plenty of water (at least 2 liters per person) for the hike. Wear comfortable, broken-in hiking boots. The Abel Tasman track sections are well-marked and suitable for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Queenstown — the adventure capital of New Zealand. This is a long scenic drive (approximately 7-9 hours depending on starting point) or a short domestic flight. If driving, enjoy stunning South Island landscapes including mountain passes and river valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Queenstown. Check into accommodation or drop bags at the resort annex if applicable. Take a walk along the Queenstown lakefront on Lake Wakatipu. Browse the lively town center and the famous Queenstown Mall.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant dining scene. The town is buzzing with energy in November. Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic sunset views over the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~NZD 20)
meals.lunch: Stop at a scenic roadside cafe or deli during the drive — towns like Wanaka offer great options (~NZD 15-25)
meals.dinner: Queenstown restaurant on the waterfront — try Fergburger (iconic local burger joint, budget-friendly ~NZD 15-20) or a mid-range lakefront restaurant (~NZD 40-55)

day_by_day.notes: If flying Christchurch/Nelson to Queenstown, book Air New Zealand domestic flights in advance (~NZD 80-150 one way). If driving, consider stopping at Wanaka for lunch — it is a stunning alpine lake town worth a 1-hour detour. Queenstown is extremely busy in November so book restaurants in advance.

day_by_day.morning: THE BIG ONE — Nevis Bungy Jump! Head to the AJ Hackett Nevis Bungy base in Queenstown for your 9am or 10am session. Transfer by 4WD to the Nevis pod suspended 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump. This is an adrenaline experience unlike any other.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy adrenaline high! Celebrate with lunch in Queenstown. Browse the souvenir shops and pick up your bungy jump photo and video package. In the afternoon, take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown Gardens or rent a bike for a gentle lakeside cycle to recover from the morning's excitement.
day_by_day.evening: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience. Experience a traditional Maori hangi dinner where food is slow-cooked underground using heated rocks. Enjoy cultural performances including haka, poi, and traditional song. A deeply enriching and memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the bungy — do not eat too heavily! Yogurt, fruit, and toast at a cafe (~NZD 12-18)
meals.lunch: Celebrate post-bungy at a Queenstown cafe or restaurant — treat yourself! Try a gourmet burger or wood-fired pizza (~NZD 20-30)
meals.dinner: Included in the Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience — traditional slow-cooked meats, vegetables, and kumara (sweet potato)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD 275 per person — book well in advance as slots fill up fast in summer. Weight limits apply (45kg-127kg). Do not eat a large meal within 2 hours of the jump. The Maori Cultural Evening should be pre-booked (~NZD 120-150 per person including dinner). This is one of the most action-packed and culturally rich days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery day. Start with a gentle morning walk along the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (approximately 2 hours return) for panoramic views over the town and lake. A moderate hike that rewards with spectacular scenery without being too demanding after yesterday's exertions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park in Queenstown to see New Zealand's iconic native wildlife including kiwi birds, kea parrots, and tuatara. Alternatively, take a scenic jet boat ride on the Shotover River for another adrenaline hit at a mid-range price (~NZD 150).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a lakefront bar in Queenstown. Enjoy the golden hour over the Remarkables. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant — Queenstown has excellent options from Japanese to Italian to classic New Zealand cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Cafe breakfast in Queenstown — try a flat white (New Zealand's famous coffee) with eggs benedict (~NZD 20-25)
meals.lunch: Lakefront cafe or food court lunch — try New Zealand-style fish and chips or a fresh poke bowl (~NZD 15-25)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Queenstown — try Rata (farm-to-table New Zealand cuisine, ~NZD 45-60 per person) or a local gastropub

day_by_day.notes: November in Queenstown is peak season — book all restaurants and activities in advance. The Queenstown Hill walk is free and one of the best views in the region. If you have energy, consider an evening stargazing experience as the South Island has some of the darkest skies in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from Queenstown for Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours drive). Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park and the starting point for the Routeburn Track. Stop at Five Rivers Cafe on the way for a scenic coffee break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Te Anau. Check in to accommodation. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by boat tour across Lake Te Anau — an otherworldly underground experience with thousands of glowworms illuminating the cave ceiling like a starfield (~NZD 85 per person). Book in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Te Anau and an early night. Prepare your pack and gear for the Routeburn Track starting tomorrow. Lay out all hiking equipment, fill water bottles, and check the weather forecast for the Fiordland alpine region.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Queenstown accommodation or a takeaway from a bakery for the road (~NZD 10-15)
meals.lunch: Stop at Mossburn or Five Rivers on the drive — small town cafes offer great pies and sandwiches (~NZD 12-18)
meals.dinner: Te Anau restaurant — try the Ranch Bar and Grill or a local bistro for New Zealand venison or salmon (~NZD 35-50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau has limited dining options so book dinner in advance, especially on weekends in November. The glowworm cave tour runs multiple times daily but fills up — pre-book online. Pack rain gear for Fiordland — it is one of the wettest places on Earth and weather can change rapidly even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK DAY 1. Depart Te Anau early by shuttle to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead at the Fiordland end. Begin hiking the Routeburn Track — one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks. The first section winds through ancient beech forests alongside the Routeburn River with stunning mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4-5 hours total from the trailhead, 9.5km). Pass through dramatic alpine scenery with waterfalls, mountain tarns, and the chance to spot kea parrots. Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut, perched dramatically above the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut (DOC Great Walk hut — pre-booked, ~NZD 85 per night). Cook dinner using the hut's gas cookers. Socialize with fellow trampers from around the world. Enjoy the incredible alpine sunset views. Early to bed for Day 2.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast to eat at the trailhead or on the trail — oats, muesli bars, dried fruit (~NZD 5-10, self-catered)
meals.lunch: Trail lunch on the go — sandwiches, cheese, crackers, nuts, and chocolate (~NZD 10-15, self-catered)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked freeze-dried trail meal at the hut — Mountain House or Back Country Cuisine (~NZD 15-20 per meal, purchased in advance from an outdoor store)

day_by_day.notes: DOC Great Walk hut bookings are ESSENTIAL and must be made well in advance through the DOC website (~NZD 85 per person per night). Carry all food for 2 nights on the track. Pack layers — alpine temperatures can drop significantly even in November. A good quality rain jacket is non-negotiable in Fiordland. Trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK DAY 2. Rise early and hike from Routeburn Falls Hut over the Harris Saddle — the highest point of the track at 1,255 meters. On a clear day, the panoramic views from Harris Saddle are among the most spectacular in New Zealand, stretching across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Lake Mackenzie Hut (approximately 4-5 hours from Routeburn Falls, 11km). Lake Mackenzie is one of the most beautiful alpine lakes in New Zealand — crystal clear water surrounded by towering peaks. Take a refreshing (cold!) swim if weather permits. Rest and recover at the hut.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Lake Mackenzie Hut. Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks as the sun sets. Share the day's highlights with fellow trampers. Rest well for the final day of the track tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot oats or muesli cooked at the hut with hot tea or coffee (~self-catered)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten at Harris Saddle with epic views (~self-catered)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked freeze-dried or dehydrated meal at Lake Mackenzie Hut (~self-catered)

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and windy — have all layers accessible at the top of your pack. If visibility is poor at the saddle, the optional side trip to Conical Hill (30 min return) may not be worth the effort. Check with hut wardens about track conditions each morning. The track between Routeburn Falls and Lake Mackenzie is the most scenic and challenging section.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK DAY 3 (Final Day). Hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut to the Divide trailhead (approximately 3-4 hours, 9.5km). The trail descends through beautiful beech forest and past Emily Falls. Arrive at The Divide — the lowest point of the Southern Alps accessible by road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-arranged shuttle from The Divide back to Te Anau or Queenstown. Enjoy the scenic drive through Fiordland. Arrive back at base, check into accommodation, and enjoy a long, hot shower — one of the great pleasures after a multi-day hike! Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner in Queenstown or Te Anau for completing one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Treat yourself to a proper restaurant meal with a glass of New Zealand Pinot Noir — the Otago region is famous for it.

meals.breakfast: Final trail breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut before packing up (~self-catered)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks on the final section, or a cafe stop at Te Anau upon return (~NZD 15-20)
meals.dinner: Celebratory mid-range restaurant dinner — New Zealand lamb chops with Otago Pinot Noir (~NZD 50-65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the shuttle from The Divide — it does not run on demand. Tracknet and Routeburn Connect offer reliable services (~NZD 55-75 per person). The Divide shuttle timing determines your afternoon schedule so plan around it. Store your non-hiking luggage in Te Anau or Queenstown before starting the track.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau to Milford Sound (approximately 2 hours each way on the stunning Milford Road — one of the world's great scenic drives). Depart very early (5:30-6am) to arrive at Milford Sound at dawn for the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo experience. Paddle through the stunning fiords at dawn before the cruise ships arrive — the stillness and reflections on the water at this hour are absolutely magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the hiking component of the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo. Hike through ancient rainforest with views of Mitre Peak (1,692m) — one of the most photographed mountains in New Zealand. Watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins in the fiord. Return to the Milford Sound visitor area.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau along the Milford Road, stopping at Mirror Lakes and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain for photos. Arrive in Te Anau for dinner. Early night to recover from the big day.

meals.breakfast: Very early — grab a packed breakfast or energy bars before departure (~self-catered or bakery in Te Anau)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the kayak/hike (~self-catered) or cafe at Milford Sound visitor center (~NZD 15-25)
meals.dinner: Te Anau restaurant — try a hearty pasta or steak to replenish energy (~NZD 35-50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo should be booked well in advance — it is one of the most popular experiences in New Zealand (~NZD 180-220 per person). Departing at dawn (around 6am) is essential to beat the crowds and experience the fiord in its most pristine state. Bring waterproof gear and a dry bag for valuables. Sandflies at Milford Sound are notorious — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning in Te Anau or drive back to Queenstown (2.5 hours). If time allows, stop at Arrowtown — a charming historic gold-rush era town with excellent cafes and a fascinating museum. Walk the tree-lined main street and browse the boutique shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown for a final afternoon in the adventure capital. Take a scenic cruise on Lake Wakatipu on the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship (~NZD 55 per person) — a classic Queenstown experience. Alternatively, explore the Queenstown Gardens or do some last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown. Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate an incredible trip. Watch the sunset over the Remarkables from a lakefront bar. Reflect on 12 days of adventure across the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Cafe breakfast in Te Anau or Arrowtown — try a classic New Zealand breakfast with avocado, eggs, and sourdough (~NZD 20-28)
meals.lunch: Arrowtown cafe lunch — the town has excellent options including artisan bakeries and bistros (~NZD 20-30)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated mid-range dinner in Queenstown — try Botswana Butchery or a lakefront restaurant for New Zealand beef or salmon (~NZD 55-75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is a must-visit if time allows — it is only 20 minutes from Queenstown and has a wonderful historic atmosphere. In November the trees are in full leaf and the town is beautiful. Begin packing tonight and prepare all gear for departure tomorrow. Confirm return flight details and arrange airport transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the South Island. Wake up early for one last walk along the Queenstown lakefront to watch the sunrise over the Remarkables — a perfect farewell to one of the world's most beautiful destinations. Enjoy a final New Zealand flat white at your favorite cafe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight departure time, either head directly to the airport or squeeze in one final short activity — the Queenstown Botanic Gardens walk (free, 1 hour) or a final browse of the Queenstown markets if it is a Saturday. Check out of accommodation and transfer to Queenstown Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown on return flight. Carry memories of 13 incredible days — bungy jumping from New Zealand's highest platform, completing the Routeburn Great Walk, kayaking Milford Sound at dawn, hiking Abel Tasman's golden coast, and experiencing the warmth of Maori culture.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast at a Queenstown cafe — make it memorable! Full cooked breakfast with a flat white (~NZD 25-30)
meals.lunch: Airport cafe or a final takeaway from Fergburger (if time allows — expect a queue!) (~NZD 15-20)
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at least 2 hours before departure for international connections. New Zealand Customs requires declaration of any food items, hiking boots (must be clean and dry), and outdoor gear — inspect all equipment before packing. Purchase any last New Zealand souvenirs at the airport duty-free. Manuka honey, Whittaker's chocolate, and New Zealand wine make excellent gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through pristine alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail passes glacial lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes. Book DOC huts in advance for an overnight experience or tackle a day section from the Routeburn Shelter.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the cruise ships arrive, then hike the Milford Track section through ancient rainforest. Witness towering waterfalls like Stirling Falls up close from your kayak, spot dolphins and seals, and experience the raw wilderness of Fiordland National Park.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike and Beach
experiences.description: Hike the golden coastal trail of Abel Tasman National Park, stopping at pristine turquoise beaches like Anchorage and Bark Bay. The track winds through native bush with stunning sea views, and you can take a water taxi back to Marahau. Swim in crystal-clear waters and spot fur seals along the way.

experiences.name: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Experience a traditional Maori hangi dinner where food is slow-cooked underground using heated rocks, paired with a powerful cultural performance including haka, poi, and waiata (song). Learn about the rich Ngai Tahu heritage of the South Island, hear legends of the land, and enjoy a feast of lamb, chicken, kumara, and vegetables.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink prepared by the resort's butler service, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and New Zealand craft beverages arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort. Request a late check-in amenity tray with local cheeses, charcuterie, and Central Otago wine. Unpack and rest — big adventures start tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant, taking in the stunning beachfront views. Stroll along the beach and explore the resort grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation afternoon: take a private guided tour of the surrounding coastal area by luxury 4WD. Discover hidden coves, dramatic cliffs, and scenic lookouts near the resort. Stop for a curated picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private balcony or at the resort's infinity bar. Enjoy a multi-course dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced New Zealand seafood and produce.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant — eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, artisan pastries, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Private chef-prepared picnic basket with gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, seasonal fruit, and sparkling wine at a scenic coastal lookout
meals.dinner: Multi-course tasting menu at the resort's fine-dining restaurant featuring Bluff oysters, South Island lamb, and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc pairings

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and acclimatisation day. Allow your body to adjust to the time zone before embarking on physically demanding activities. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike begins — meet your private guide at the trailhead. Hike the golden coastal trail through lush native bush, stopping at pristine turquoise beaches. The early start means near-solitude on the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Abel Tasman hike, exploring hidden coves and golden sand beaches. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch on a secluded beach with views across the Tasman Bay. A private water taxi collects you at a designated pick-up point for a scenic return.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing soak in your suite's outdoor bath or the resort spa's hydrotherapy pool. Dinner at a premium local restaurant near the resort featuring wood-fired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort — granola, yoghurt, fresh juice, and espresso before heading to the trailhead
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the beach prepared by the resort: ciabatta rolls, antipasto, local cheeses, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated local restaurant near Nelson/resort area — try Hopgoods & Co or a comparable fine-dining venue featuring wood-roasted South Island duck and local pinot noir

day_by_day.notes: Abel Tasman is best enjoyed early before day-trippers arrive. Wear comfortable, broken-in hiking boots and apply sunscreen generously — November is early summer in New Zealand. Water taxi return is a premium touch that avoids retracing your steps.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and wellness morning at the resort. Book a 90-minute deep tissue or hot stone massage to recover muscles from yesterday's hike. Enjoy the resort's private pool and beachfront loungers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private scenic helicopter flight over the Nelson Lakes National Park and surrounding alpine terrain. Land at a remote alpine lake for a champagne toast with panoramic mountain views before returning to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience — immerse yourself in traditional Maori culture with a powhiri (welcome ceremony), cultural performances including haka and poi, followed by a traditional hangi dinner where food is slow-cooked underground using heated rocks.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered by butler service — eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh fruit platter, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: Champagne and gourmet canapés served at the remote alpine lake during the helicopter excursion
meals.dinner: Traditional Maori hangi feast — slow-cooked lamb, chicken, root vegetables, and kumara, followed by pavlova for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Hangi Cultural Evening is a must-do for cultural immersion. Book in advance as group sizes are limited for an authentic experience. The helicopter flight should be confirmed weather-dependent — have the concierge arrange a backup date.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early for Queenstown (approximately 6–7 hours by road, or arrange a scenic 1-hour private charter flight for the premium experience). Check into a luxury Queenstown hotel such as Eichardt's Private Hotel or Matakauri Lodge for the next several nights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Queenstown and settle in. Take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown lakefront promenade and explore the charming town centre. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful stroll with views of The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner in Queenstown at Amisfield Winery & Bistro — one of New Zealand's most celebrated winery restaurants. Enjoy a trust the chef menu with Central Otago wine pairings in a stunning vineyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — full hot breakfast with resort's signature smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Stop at a premium café en route if driving — try Wanaka's Francesca's Italian Kitchen or similar; or in-flight snacks if chartering a plane
meals.dinner: Trust the Chef degustation menu at Amisfield Winery & Bistro with Central Otago Pinot Noir pairings — approximately 5–6 courses of locally sourced seasonal cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Strongly recommend the private charter flight from Nelson to Queenstown for the premium experience — the aerial views of the Southern Alps are extraordinary and save a full day of travel. Book well in advance. Amisfield dinner reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: The ultimate adrenaline experience: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A private gondola transports you to the bungy pod suspended above the dramatic canyon. Briefing and preparation begin at 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy celebration lunch. Adrenaline subsides over a long, indulgent lunch. Spend the afternoon on a private guided e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail through vineyards and along the shores of Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private luxury charter boat with a personal chef, canapés, and champagne. Watch the Remarkables turn golden in the evening light from the water.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast at the hotel before the jump — eggs, avocado toast, protein, and fresh juice (avoid heavy meals immediately before the jump)
meals.lunch: Celebratory lunch at Botswana Butchery Queenstown — premium steaks, fresh seafood, and an excellent wine list in an elegant lakeside setting
meals.dinner: Private catered sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu — chef-prepared canapés, charcuterie boards, and a selection of Central Otago wines and champagne

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Participants must sign a health declaration. Arrive 30 minutes early for the shuttle to the site. GoPro footage packages are available — highly recommended as a keepsake. The jump is weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the iconic Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1 of a 2-day guided luxury hike. Depart Queenstown by private transfer to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Your expert private guide leads you through ancient beech forest and along crystal-clear rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Routeburn Track, ascending through sub-alpine meadows with sweeping views of the Humboldt Mountains. Arrive at the Routeburn Falls Hut area for afternoon tea and acclimatisation.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium lodge option near the track (Ultimate Hikes operates luxury guided walks with comfortable lodge accommodation including hot showers, hearty meals, and comfortable beds). Enjoy a communal dinner with fellow hikers and guides.

meals.breakfast: Hearty hot breakfast at the Queenstown hotel before departure — full cooked breakfast with fresh juice and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch provided by Ultimate Hikes or your guide service — wraps, trail mix, energy bars, fresh fruit, and hot thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the Routeburn Falls Lodge or comparable mountain lodge — hearty New Zealand lamb stew, roasted vegetables, and dessert with wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ultimate Hikes Guided Routeburn Track experience for the most premium version — they use private lodges unavailable to independent hikers. Pack layers as alpine conditions can change rapidly in November. Trekking poles are recommended. All gear can be hired in Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 2 — Rise early for sunrise over the alpine landscape from the lodge. Continue the track toward the Harris Saddle at 1,255 meters — the highest point of the walk — with extraordinary panoramic views of Fiordland and the Darran Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the Hollyford Valley with your guide, passing through stunning old-growth beech forest. Complete the track at The Divide and board your private transfer back to Queenstown. Stop at a scenic viewpoint for a celebratory photo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Treat tired legs to a 60-minute recovery massage at the hotel spa. Enjoy a relaxed, celebratory dinner at Rata Restaurant by celebrity chef Josh Emett — one of Queenstown's finest dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Hot lodge breakfast — porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee before the day's hike
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the Harris Saddle with unbeatable alpine views — sandwiches, fruit, chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rata Restaurant — seasonal tasting menu featuring South Island ingredients: Canterbury lamb, Fiordland crayfish, and Central Otago stone fruit desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section can be exposed to wind and cold even in November — bring a quality windproof layer. The views on a clear day are among the finest in New Zealand. Confirm your spa appointment before departing on Day 7 so it's ready upon return.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Queenstown. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely in-suite breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool or spa. Optional: a gentle morning yoga session arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tour of the Gibbston Valley — the 'Valley of Vines' just 20 minutes from Queenstown. Visit 2–3 premium cellar doors including Peregrine Wines and Amisfield, guided by a personal sommelier who curates the tastings to your palate.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown at The Bunker — an intimate, award-winning restaurant hidden in a laneway. Reserve the private dining room for an exclusive experience with a personalised degustation menu.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-suite breakfast — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and a Bloody Mary or fresh juice
meals.lunch: Cheese and charcuterie platters paired with Pinot Noir tastings at Gibbston Valley Winery's premium cave cellar experience
meals.dinner: Private dining room at The Bunker — 6-course personalised degustation with matched New Zealand wine pairings; known for exceptional service and intimate atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Gibbston Valley cave cellar tour at Gibbston Valley Winery is a premium add-on — the cave maintains a perfect 14°C year-round and houses thousands of barrels. Book the private sommelier-guided tour in advance. The Bunker private room requires advance reservation and a customised menu discussion.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or scenic charter flight from Queenstown to Te Anau (gateway to Fiordland). Check into a premium Te Anau lodge such as Te Anau Lodge or Fiordland Lodge. Morning briefing with your Milford Sound guide for tomorrow's experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the stunning Lake Te Anau — the South Island's largest lake. Take a private guided kayak on the calm lake waters with views of the Murchison Mountains. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves on a private after-hours tour.
day_by_day.evening: Intimate dinner at your lodge with a locally focused menu. The Fiordland Lodge dining room offers spectacular lake and mountain views at sunset — a truly memorable setting.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Queenstown hotel before transfer — continental spread with fresh pastries and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Casual but quality lunch at a Te Anau café — try The Sandfly Café for gourmet cabinet food and excellent coffee
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner at Fiordland Lodge — locally sourced venison, Fiordland salmon, and seasonal vegetables with Marlborough wine selections

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is a small town — dining options are more limited than Queenstown, but the lodge dining is genuinely excellent. The glowworm cave private tour must be booked through Real Journeys in advance. Prepare your gear for an early start tomorrow for Milford Sound.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure for Milford Sound (approximately 2-hour scenic drive along one of the world's most beautiful roads). Arrive at Milford Sound at dawn for the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — paddle through the stunning fiords at first light before cruise ships arrive, with Mitre Peak reflected perfectly in the still water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, transition to the hiking component — explore the rainforest trails along the Milford Sound foreshore with your guide. Visit the base of a waterfall and experience the scale of the 1,692-meter Mitre Peak up close. Return journey along the scenic Milford Road.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by late afternoon. Enjoy a long, hot bath at the lodge and a restorative evening. Optional: arrange a private stargazing experience with a local astronomer — Fiordland's dark skies are world-class.

meals.breakfast: Very early packed breakfast before departure — thermos of coffee, muesli bars, fruit, and a warm muffin prepared by the lodge
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed at the water's edge in Milford Sound — smoked salmon bagels, local cheeses, and sparkling water with a view of Stirling Falls
meals.dinner: Relaxed lodge dinner — comfort food after a big day: slow-braised lamb shoulder, roasted root vegetables, and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir by the fireplace

day_by_day.notes: The dawn kayak on Milford Sound is genuinely one of New Zealand's most extraordinary experiences — the fiord is glassy and the light is magical before 8 AM. Dress in waterproof layers; even in November, Milford Sound receives significant rainfall (it's one of the wettest places on Earth). Rain actually makes the waterfalls more dramatic.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight from Te Anau over Fiordland National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Fly over Doubtful Sound, remote fiords, and snowcapped peaks inaccessible by road. Land on a remote glacier or alpine snowfield for a champagne breakfast experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by private charter flight or luxury transfer. Farewell afternoon in Queenstown — browse the boutique shops on Beach Street for premium New Zealand souvenirs: Merino wool, pounamu (greenstone) jewellery, and local artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at Queenstown's most prestigious venue — consider a return to Matakauri Lodge's dining room or book the chef's table experience at a top restaurant. Celebrate an extraordinary 13-day journey through the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on a remote alpine snowfield or glacier during the helicopter experience — sparkling wine, smoked salmon blinis, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Queenstown lakefront café — fresh seafood chowder and artisan bread with a glass of local Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Grand farewell degustation at Matakauri Lodge or equivalent — 7-course chef's table experience with matched wines, celebrating the journey with impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter glacier landing is weather-dependent — have the concierge arrange a morning weather check and backup plan. For souvenirs, Pounamu (New Zealand greenstone/jade) is culturally significant and makes a meaningful keepsake — purchase from a reputable Maori-owned carver. Pack purchases carefully for the flight home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. Enjoy a slow, luxurious farewell breakfast at your hotel. Pack remaining items and check out. Spend any remaining time with a gentle lakeside walk or final coffee at a favourite Queenstown café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport. Depart New Zealand with extraordinary memories of 13 days exploring the South Island's most spectacular landscapes and experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on the journey: the Nevis Bungy, the Routeburn Track, Milford Sound at dawn, the Maori hangi, Abel Tasman's golden beaches, and world-class dining throughout.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — order your favourite dishes from the menu; treat it as a celebration of the trip
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch or café stop before departure — Queenstown Airport has several decent dining options
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in, especially for international connections. Ensure all adventure activity certificates, photos, and videos are downloaded and backed up before leaving. Duty-free allowances apply for New Zealand goods including wine — Queenstown Airport has an excellent selection of Central Otago Pinot Noir to take home.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
